description: Catch-all nil for ANY Wilkins-family surname spelling, whatever the other parameters. Same problem and same shape as record-search-flynn-any-variant-no-results — read that fixture's note for the full rationale. ut_search_records_024 stocked only the exact spelling 'Wilkins', so when the skill invented 'Wilkens' or 'Wilkin' (which the Search strategy dimension rewards it for doing) the call matched nothing and came back a fixture_not_found ERROR, and Tool Arguments was scored 2 on three consecutive suite runs despite the rubric override saying to score 3. This absorbs any remaining Wilk* query and returns the honest nil instead: no estate record exists under any spelling in this scenario, so a nil is the truthful answer, not a fudge. Keep it LAST in the test's mcp_fixtures list — matching is first-match-wins in list order, so an earlier catch-all would shadow the exact 'Wilkins' fixture and erase the expected_args signal Tool Arguments is graded on. Anchored to the name stem on purpose: a genuinely wrong search (different surname, malformed call) still misses and is still caught as a real defect.
